clue.text: I’ve no idea if cashmere runs

indicators.note: dye that runs spreads out of place, so the word before it loses its order

blocks.note: taken as written, eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs when asked whether a cashmere jumper will bleed in the wash.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a casual spoken way of saying you have no clue, a shrugging reply to a question.

clue.text: Spot in which dog’s unlikely to get loose?

indicators.note: the second word sits inside the first, as something kept within an enclosure

blocks.note: to spot something is to see it
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A question about a fenced yard where a dog cannot escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' looks like a place or a dog's name, but it is a verb for noticing; the dog sits inside it to give SE-CUR-E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something firmly fastened or safely held is not going to come free, which is the adjective's basic meaning.

clue.text: A body of water in a foreign country

blocks.note: taken as written
a broad is a lake, as in the Norfolk Broads, a waterway district of eastern England

explanation.surface: A lake or sea somewhere overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes being overseas or away from home, exactly as the prepositional phrase does.

clue.text: Mines may close up around October’s end

indicators.note: things that are up in the air or disordered are churned, so the words before are mixed
the mixed letters go round the following letter, enclosing it
the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the final letter of the month's name

explanation.surface: A warning that minefields may be shut down at the end of October.
explanation.walkthrough: A claymore is both a Scottish broadsword and a type of directional anti-personnel mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Claymores are a named model of directional landmine used by the military, so the plural is an example of mines.

clue.text: Court shames Ohio union criminal

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so the letters before it are twisted out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
O. is the old postal abbreviation for the American state
taken as written

explanation.surface: A judge disgraces a corrupt labour union from Ohio.
explanation.walkthrough: Mansion House is the official residence of the Lord Mayor of London, which long housed its own justice room and magistrates' court.
explanation.definitionFit: The London building held a magistrates' bench where the Lord Mayor heard cases, so it served as a court of law.

clue.text: Stuff is ace with money to burn mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the phrase's word is dropped

blocks.note: ace and fab are both slang for excellent
someone with money to burn is wealthy

explanation.surface: Boasting that it is great to have cash so plentiful you could set fire to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloth or material is called stuff in older usage, and woven material is the textile sense of the answer.

clue.text: A warplane over China

blocks.note: taken as written
a MiG is a Russian fighter jet
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A military jet flying over the country of China.
explanation.walkthrough: China is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate rhymes with mate, so it means a friend, not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for a friend or pal: one from Spanish, one from London rhyming slang.

clue.text: Distress irate dad showed to a great degree

indicators.note: to distress something is to rough it up, so the following words are knocked into new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An angry father made his upset very obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: To radiate a feeling, such as confidence or happiness, is to give it off strongly so everybody notices.

clue.text: Associates of Johnson, Gove and Hunt?

blocks.clueFragment: Associates of Johnson, Gove and Hunt?
blocks.note: surface reading: political allies of three well-known Conservative politicians
setter's reading: the three are examples of Con (Conservative) types, so read the phrase as kinds of Con

explanation.surface: Who are the friends of three senior Tory politicians?
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Johnson, Michael Gove and Jeremy Hunt are Conservative ministers; CON is the abbreviation, and SORTS are types, so CON-SORTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Consorts are partners or companions, people one keeps company with, so the plural noun fits associates.

clue.text: Death cover’s pointless in the end

indicators.note: the end of the word is its last letter, so only that one is taken

blocks.note: a curtain covers a window
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A burial shroud turns out to be useless after all.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for has: the cover has the last letter of pointless added.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying it is curtains for someone is an idiom meaning the end, so it stands for death or ruin.

clue.text: Oh, I’d deny penning this type of clue

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the words before it hold the solution inside them

blocks.note: the run of letters after the opening O and before the final Y

explanation.surface: Someone protests that they never wrote a clue of this kind.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue describes itself: it is an example of the very kind it names.
explanation.definitionFit: A clue whose answer lies concealed within consecutive letters of its wording is the name crossword solvers use for this kind.

clue.text: Go for it and push the Queen?

blocks.note: first meaning: take decisive action at last
second meaning: in chess, advancing a piece is taking your turn

explanation.surface: An encouragement to shove the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen is a chess piece, not the monarch; pushing it is playing your turn.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to act decisively, often romantically, and literally describes taking a turn in a board game.

clue.text: River near tree bordering a field

indicators.note: near means next to, so the first piece sits right beside the rest
to border something is to surround its edges, so the tree goes round the next word

blocks.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
an elm is a tree
taken as written

explanation.surface: A river runs beside a tree at the edge of a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: A field of study or activity is a sphere or domain, which is the figurative sense of a kingdom.

clue.text: Very soon squeal meeting old lover boy

blocks.note: in a mo, short for in a moment
to squeal on someone is to inform, or rat
O is a standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Soon someone will grass on an ex-boyfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian loan word means a male sweetheart or admirer, the masculine of a woman beloved.

clue.text: Royal creep renting Rolls

indicators.note: something that rolls tumbles over, so the letters before it are turned about

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An unpleasant person hires a Rolls-Royce car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolls' reads as the car, Rolls-Royce, but it is the verb signalling a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The title went to George IV while he ruled for his ill father, so he is an example of a royal.

clue.text: Choose Wagner’s last lyrical work for conductor

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the composer's name alone

blocks.note: to elect is to choose
the final letter of the name
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: Picking a Wagner finale as a showpiece for an orchestra's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' looks musical beside Wagner, but it is the electrical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is a terminal through which current passes, so it conducts electricity in the physics sense.

clue.text: Those at helm of fish-catching ship

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it, so the ship surrounds the fish

blocks.note: SS is the prefix for steamship
a kipper is a smoked herring

explanation.surface: The captains of a trawler.
explanation.definitionFit: Captains of boats steer or command the vessel, so they are the ones at the wheel.

clue.text: Crack in a vessel

blocks.note: a and one both mean a single thing
a liner is an ocean ship

explanation.surface: A split appears in a pot or ship's hull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like a fracture in the vessel, but it is a quip.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack can mean a witty remark, and a short joke delivered in a single sentence is just that.

clue.text: Top lawyer? Sign one’s luck changed?

indicators.note: something changed is altered, so the letters before it are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A senior barrister wonders whether a signature has altered their fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a King's Counsel is a senior barrister appointed by the Crown.
explanation.definitionFit: The title marks a barrister of high rank in Britain and Commonwealth courts, so the question mark flags an example.

clue.text: Creature comfort wife left outside

indicators.note: outside means on the edges, so the two short pieces wrap round the comfort word

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife
ease is comfort or relief
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A spouse is left out in the cold without any home comforts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creature comfort' reads as one phrase, but it splits into the definition and a separate word.
explanation.definitionFit: A weasel is a small carnivorous animal, and any animal is a creature.

clue.text: Race around Kent area presents problem

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the race word wraps round the area

blocks.note: to tear is to rush or race
Kent is a county in the south-east of England, SE

explanation.surface: A fast drive round the county of Kent causes difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaser is a puzzle or tricky question, a brainteaser, so it is a kind of problem.

clue.text: We often criticise European films

definitions.note: a sentence the answer would speak, rather than a plural noun

blocks.note: a Pole is a person from Poland
a film is a thin haze, as mists are

explanation.surface: Critics complain that they often pan European cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Films' suggests cinema, but it means thin layers of haze.
explanation.definitionFit: Polemists are writers of polemics, aggressive arguments attacking opinions, so they could say this of themselves.

clue.text: One employed to style The Stones?

definitions.text: One employed to style The Stones?

blocks.clueFragment: One employed to style The Stones?
blocks.note: surface reading: a hairdresser or stylist hired by the Rolling Stones rock band
setter's reading: someone paid to dress and shape blocks of stone in building

explanation.walkthrough: The capitals suggest the Rolling Stones, a British rock band; the answer is a craftsperson working with stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoneworker cuts, dresses and lays building blocks, so shaping stones is literally the trade.

clue.text: Article about initially exciting male topic

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the following word is taken
about means turned round, so the two short pieces after it are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the definite article
the first letter of the word
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about a thrilling man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like a newspaper piece; it is the grammatical word THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject a talk or essay is about, so it is a synonym for topic.

clue.text: Man, that sounds serious!

indicators.note: sounds points to how a word is heard rather than how it is spelt

blocks.note: earnest means serious and sincere

explanation.surface: An exclamation at hearing something grave.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest plays on this same pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest is a boy's given name, and crosswords use man to stand for any male first name.

clue.text: Giant deficit breaks firm associated with America

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so the deficit goes into the firm

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
a deficit is a shortfall or loss
the United States

explanation.surface: A shortfall ruins an American company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giant' looks like an adjective for the deficit, but it is a noun for the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A colossus is a huge statue or anything of enormous size, so it is a giant.

clue.text: Beach kiosk stuffed with rubbish primarily

indicators.note: something stuffed has a filling put inside it
primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: a kiosk is a stand or stall
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A seaside stall crammed with litter.
explanation.definitionFit: Strand is a literary word for the shore, the land along the edge of the sea.

clue.text: Outing-organiser always knocked back beer and drop of red

indicators.note: knocked back means pushed backwards, so the word before it is read right to left
a drop is the tiniest amount, so only the first letter of the colour is taken

blocks.note: ever means always
ale is a beer
the opening letter of the colour

explanation.surface: A trip planner always downs a beer and a little red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' and 'beer' suggest drinking, but the first means turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Outing someone means exposing a secret about them, so the person who discloses it is one who reveals.
